summary: Holonet is the in-world communication layer: GM-only serialized world-setting storage, exactly-once publication, hook-driven notification emitters, Intel, secret notes, the Job board, and player trades and payouts. Credit deltas go through TransactionEngine with whitelisted holonet-* contexts, and the TI4-C0 rule that indeterminate outcomes are never auto-compensated is implemented and tested. Main problems: (1) multi-step trades and payouts get atomicity from Holonet's own snapshot and compensating-restore mechanism rather than an engine transaction. Rollback overwrites the whole actor and deletes and recreates every item without keepId, so item ids can change and concurrent changes can be lost. (2) The Party Fund is a credit pool and ledger in world settings outside TransactionEngine. An owner-approved workflow (V-P6C-19) conflicts with the OSI no-parallel-ledger rule. (3) holonet-messenger-service.js is 7,055 SLOC across seven responsibilities; seams are proposed. (4) The droid, ship and follower HP emitters test flattened keys on the expanded diff object and never fire. scripts/holonet/scripts/** is a stale, broken copy of core init.

findings.title: holonet-messenger-service.js mixes seven responsibilities in 7,055 SLOC
findings.observed: The largest runtime module in the repo, with about 100 static methods. _gmThreadAction (:4421-4935) is a ~500-line action switch. View-model builders (:1911-2484) sit beside credit settlement and rollback code. ui-shell depends on it heavily (88 edges into holonet).
findings.intendedOwnership: Seams: S1 MessengerThreadService (:1618-1930, :3608-3784, :7559-7593); S2 HolonetJobBoardService (:2704-3377, :4935-5078); S3 HolonetSecretNoteService (:3377-3608); S4 HolonetTradeService (:3918-4412, :5573-7501); S5 HolonetRewardSettlementService (:5078-5511); S6 MessengerViewModelBuilder (:1911-2484, pure); S7 Party Fund adapter (:213-225, :5777-5958). _gmThreadAction becomes a dispatcher.
findings.proposedSolution: Extract S6 first (pure, lowest risk), then S3 and S2, then S4/S5 after F-HOL-002 is decided. Keep HolonetMessengerService as a thin facade so the 19 consumers are unchanged.
findings.alternatives: Extract S4/S5 directly into TransactionEngine-backed services if F-HOL-002 option (a) is chosen.
findings.regressionTests: Existing ti4c0-g16/g26 and gm-holonet-* tests plus per-seam unit tests.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Messenger smoke test after each extraction.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Independent ownership for jobs, trades, notes and view models.
findings.risk: Medium; credit paths are in scope.

findings.title: Trade/payout rollback is a parallel atomicity engine using whole-actor overwrite and item delete-and-recreate
findings.observed: When a multi-actor trade or job payout fails, Holonet restores each actor from a pre-operation toObject snapshot. It overwrites name, img, system, flags, ownership and prototypeToken (with skipValidation), deletes all current items and recreates them from the snapshot through ActorEngine.createEmbeddedDocuments with no keepId option. Effects get the same treatment. Results: (a) item and effect ids are expected to change, breaking id references such as equipped slots or upgrade links (Foundry default behavior, FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED); (b) any concurrent change to those actors (HP, conditions, other transactions) is silently reverted; (c) restore success is not verified (CR-HOL-02). This duplicates the exact-snapshot transactional rollback already in ActorEngine.applyMutationPlan / TransactionEngine (TI4-C0 G06-S1). Only the rollback path is affected; the success path is not.
findings.intendedOwnership: OSI / A-10: TransactionEngine owns atomic trades (credits, item transfer, approval, rollback).
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decision. (a) Move multi-actor trade/payout settlement into a TransactionEngine operation (e.g. extend executeMutationTransaction to multi-actor plans) that uses targeted inverse operations and exact verification. (b) Minimum fix: restore only the fields and items the operation touched, use keepId:true, and verify the result.
findings.alternatives: Keep the current behavior and document it as a known L3 limitation (not recommended).
findings.regressionTests: Test: forced failure mid-trade; assert item ids unchanged and unrelated actor fields untouched after rollback.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Force a counter-offer failure between two owned actors; inspect item ids and equipped state.
findings.risk: High; credit movement and item identity.

findings.title: Party Fund is a credit pool and ledger outside TransactionEngine
findings.observed: The fund balance is a world setting written with game.settings.set. Its ledger is a separate world setting truncated to 100 entries. Fund-side changes do not go through TransactionEngine; actor-side changes do. A job payout with a party cut writes the fund and then pays actors inside Holonet's own atomic wrapper.
findings.intendedOwnership: Undecided: OSI says TransactionEngine is the single source of truth with no parallel ledgers, while V-P6C-19 approves a Party Fund workflow with its own ledger entry.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decides whether the Party Fund becomes a TransactionEngine-managed account (one ledger, atomic with actor deltas) or is a documented A-10 exception. Until then, no new Party Fund writers.
findings.alternatives: Model the fund as a world 'party' actor so TransactionEngine handles it as an ordinary actor.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Party Fund contribute/charge/payout plus vehicle ammo purchase.

findings.title: Droid/ship/follower HP emitters test flattened keys and never fire
findings.observed: The updateActor hook receives the change diff as an expanded object (changes.system.hp.value). The emitters read changes['system.hp'], which is undefined for expanded diffs, so the droid and ship handlers return early and the follower check is always false. The droid emitter also requires actor.system.isDroid and actor.system.ownedBy, which were not verified against the actor schema. These listeners run on every client for every actor update while doing no work.
findings.proposedSolution: Technical defect fix: use foundry.utils.hasProperty(changes, 'system.hp.value'), gate to a single client (the active GM), and verify the droid and owner predicates against the V2 schema.
findings.alternatives: Emit from the damage/repair engines instead of observing updateActor.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test calling onUpdateActor with an expanded diff.
findings.foundryAcceptance: FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED: damage an owned droid and see the notification.
findings.risk: Low; turning on notifications could add record volume (F-HOL-008).

findings.title: Direct actor flag writes for intel locker and presence
findings.observed: actor.setFlag('foundryvtt-swse','intelLocker') and ('holonetPresence') store UI/communication metadata with no @mutation-exception comment. These are the only two probe hits in the domain, and both are real writes.
findings.proposedSolution: Same owner decision as F-MEN-001 / F-GAL-003 (metadata flag exception class vs ActorEngine flag path without recalc).
findings.alternatives: Presence could be a User flag instead of an actor flag.

findings.title: scripts/holonet/scripts/** is a stale, broken copy of core init
findings.observed: None of the four files has an importer and none is listed in system.json. init.js imports a core sidebar-structure-diagnostics module that does not exist under scripts/core, so it would fail if loaded. first-run-experience.js duplicates five exported symbols of scripts/core/first-run-experience.js (134 diff lines). the scene-controls init file is a self-declared deprecated wrapper (legacy D).
findings.intendedOwnership: Core init lives in scripts/core and index.js (infrastructure investigator).
findings.proposedSolution: Legacy C: delete the directory after a final grep of packs and macros.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes a misleading second init path.

findings.title: Unreachable badge service/renderer, delivery-state and barrels
findings.observed: Census: no runtime path (static proof, or orphan with name mentions only). Unread counts are served by HolonetMessengerService.getUnreadMessageCount.
findings.proposedSolution: Investigate the badge service against the shell unread badge; if superseded, delete it (C). Delete the barrels.

findings.title: All records and threads stored as two world-setting arrays rewritten per message
findings.observed: Each save reads the full array, edits it and rewrites the setting. Foundry broadcasts the whole setting value to every client. MessengerMaintenanceService prune/compact exists, which shows growth is a known concern.
findings.proposedSolution: Hypothesis: instrument the setting payload size and write latency in a long campaign. If material, shard by thread or move to JournalEntry documents.

findings.title: HolonetStorage imports ShellMutationGuard (UI)
findings.observed: Settings writes are wrapped only to silence the shell's dev warning.
findings.proposedSolution: Have the shell guard allow-list storage call stacks, or move the guard primitive to infrastructure.
